C-FLUSH-TWO-WAVES.Problem:
The staged buffer is the authority's hold-out area under the D30 freeze: entries staged there are not in the record until a flush lands them. Seven entries sit staged (`F230`, `F233`, `F234`, `F235`, `F236`, `F237`, `D38`, measured by parsing the buffer with the shipped `parseFrozenMarkdown`, which throws on any adjacency defect, so a clean parse is itself the adjacency check), and the flush set is all seven, split into two waves by a reason the payment machinery and the window arithmetic force:
**Wave 1 is not this bundle's payment, and the move is not optional.** `F233` and `F234` are already minted: the archived `C-TAUGHT-RULES` row's `<Pays>` names both, so the payer map claims them the moment they are live. The shipped validator refuses any committed tree holding them without the move (`finding-eligible-still-live`, driven: exactly two findings, both naming archive event `C-TAUGHT-RULES`), so their flush and their `--retire` are one execution wave, and the tree the commit holds is the moved state. Their retirement is the shipped writer's stamp derived from the payer map — the record catching up to the payment `C-TAUGHT-RULES` already delivered (its remedy shipped in PR #89, archived at this spec's base commit) — not a payment this bundle charters.
**The two-wave split is what keeps the window honest.** The live findings root reads `base="7681" headroom="165" ceiling="7846"` at this commit. The six staged findings together measure 206 element lines by the shipped counting rule — more than the window holds — and the all-six single write is refused by the shipped writer: `--rewrite-roots` exits 1 with `ceiling-exceeded` (`7887 > 7846`), nothing written, naming the genre, both counts, and the move as the remedy (driven). The wave-1-first sequencing lands `F233` and `F234` inside the window (96 ≤ 165), retires them, and re-opens the window to its held 165 before wave 2 lands `F230`, `F235`, `F236` and `F237` (110 ≤ 165, margin 55) and `D38` (36 ≤ the rulings window). Every hand write's root rewrite is therefore satisfiable at every step, and no committed state ever holds a ceiling-consuming write. The one-wave alternative the split declines is measured and recorded in Assumptions — it lands a valid record only by letting the move, not the shipped root writer, absorb an above-ceiling hand write.
**Nothing becomes eligible in wave 2, so the close's move is a no-op.** A flush that minted a row or stamped a `<PaidBy>` would leave the committed tree holding an eligible element the validator refuses. Measured at this commit: the payer map mints 87 tokens and names none of `F230`, `F235`, `F236`, `F237`, `D38`; `D38`'s rendered element carries `<Title>` and `<Body>` only — no `CodifiedIn`, no `TaughtIn`; no row is minted. The post-wave-2 validator returns zero findings (driven), and the close ceremony's own move reports `moved 0` and writes nothing (driven end to end on a faithful copy).
**The buffer's entries name their own futures, and this bundle must not swallow them.** `F235`'s owner is the record-engine bundle that next touches the engine's root resolution; `F236` and `F237` name the next teaching-surface increment; `D38` sequences a `src/` id builder across `spec new`, `supersede`, the anchor validation, the skills, the schema reference and the README — its own chartered bundle when the maintainer sequences it, never folded into a bundle in flight. The flush records them; it charters none of them.

Goals.Goal: The two-wave flush of exactly the anchors f233 and f234 (wave 1), then f230, f235, f236, f237 and d38 (wave 2) — selected by anchor id, matched as `` forms in the buffer, never by position; all seven staged entries are present and all seven land. Wave 1: two `` elements land in `docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH/findings.xml` in the house shape the predecessors calibrated (open tag, `` carrying the heading line, `<Body>` carrying the buffer body, close tag — the shipped `renderFinding` shape at `scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts:470`, which is not exported and is rendered to the same bytes by the flush), appended after the last live element and before the root close tag; two index `<Entry>` lines land in `docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH/decisions.xml` after the last existing entry; then one `--retire` reports `moved 2` and the shipped writer stamps both elements `<PaidBy>C-TAUGHT-RULES</PaidBy>` in `findings-retired.xml` and flips the two `Entry` layers to `layer="retired"` in place. Wave 2: four more `<Finding>` elements and one `<Decision>` element (the shipped `renderDecision` shape at `scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts:480`) land the same way, with five index `<Entry>` lines — `genre="finding"` for the four findings, `genre="decision"` for `d38`, derived from the existing index, each self-closing in the form ` <Entry id="…" token="…" genre="…" layer="live" />`. Bodies embed through the shipped `xmlEscape` render shape and no other transform: the decode round trip returns the staged bytes for every flushed body (driven), and the measured escape facts are in Assumptions — no render-time normalization exists, and any transform beyond the shipped escape is a deviation this spec's criteria refuse. The citation rule this bundle adopts, the predecessors': a citation that does not resolve does not enter the record — every fragment citation in the flushed bodies is measured resolvable against the index once the waves land (the shipped `validate-citation-anchors` exits 0 on the driven moved record at both the post-wave-1 and post-wave-2 states), and any staged reference the gate would not resolve is a stop-and-report, never something to normalize away at render. The roots are rewritten after each hand write by `--rewrite-roots`, the shipped writer — never by hand: it holds every persisted ceiling byte-for-byte, re-derives each `base` from the shipped metric read back, and refuses an exceeded ceiling before any write (exit 1, nothing written, naming the genre, both counts in their unit, and the move as the remedy — driven on the all-six single write). A read-back above a held ceiling stops the task and reports; it does not raise the ceiling, and it does not trim a staged body to make room. The committed sequence is: wave 1 (flush, the validator's two eligibility findings read as a working-tree state, the `--retire` in the same execution wave, validation exits 0), wave 2 (flush, `--rewrite-roots`, validation exits 0), the close (statuses `applied`, the bundle archived, one `--retire` reporting `moved 0`, validation exits 0).

The walk assertion the later plan adds, and no suite repair. The shipped `C-TAUGHT-RULES` carrier walk (`scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts`, the test whose message names the carrier relations for all six tokens) already covers `f233` and `f234` in the payment-invariant form — exactly once across the findings pair when a carrier exists, status agreeing with the holding file, `<PaidBy>C-TAUGHT-RULES</PaidBy>` when retired, the index `Entry` layer agreeing, the carrier-absent case green — and it survives wave 1's move on the production record (driven: 87 pass / 0 fail at every state of this bundle's drive). The later plan adds the same walk form, as one production assertion in `scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts`, over `f230`, `f235`, `f236`, `f237` and `d38`: each exists exactly once across its genre's pair of files (`findings.xml` and `findings-retired.xml` for the findings, `rulings.xml` and `rulings-retired.xml` for `d38`), with no fixed expectation of which file holds it, its `status` agreeing with the holding file, its token and genre agreeing, its single index `<Entry>` carrying the agreeing `genre` and a `layer` that agrees with the holding file, plus the shipped read-back arithmetic (the findings root's `base` equals the file's `newlineCount` read back and `base + headroom = ceiling`). The relation is payment-invariant by construction — a later legitimate payment of any flushed id retires the element, flips its index layer, and leaves every clause true — so the assertion adds no new liveness pin. The assertion lands with wave 2 (the wave-2 commit), so every committed state of this bundle carries a suite consistent with its own record. Shown green on the driven moved record (the walk probe written once in this form exits 0), and shown failing on mutated copies with a `<Finding>` element duplicated (the walk reads two carriers) and with a flushed element's index layer flipped against its holding file (both driven; the layer flip also reddens the shipped roots tripwire — 86 pass / 1 fail, exactly the `C-PAYMENT-RECORD-4 roots invariant`). No other suite assertion needs repair at any state: the shipped `bundleMinted` extension already carries `F233` and `F234` to `C-TAUGHT-RULES`, and no state of this bundle mints anything new (driven: 87/0 at the baseline, after wave 1's move, and after wave 2).

Constraints.Constraint: Ceremony tier T1 (module-change shape): the record the retirement validator governs, the retirement suite, and this bundle's own artifacts; no graph module is written, no `src/` file is edited, and exactly one `scripts/` file is edited (the suite: the walk assertion the Goals charter — one file, one job). Roadmap: RM-GOVERNED-PATH (record integrity). Binding live rulings: `D28` (every genre carries a retirement rule and a size ratchet — both waves land inside every persisted window; the figures live in Assumptions and expire), `D28.1` (eligibility is the enforcement and the ceiling the backstop: the wave-1 mid-state's two eligibility findings are the enforcement saying the move is due, a declared and verified working-tree state, never a commit `validate:ci` can see), `D30` (scoped, not skirted — the record is this bundle's deliverable, so the freeze is scoped to the execution window that reads or rewrites the record files: no other dispatch touches the record while a record-writing task of this bundle is in flight, and no brief promises a frozen base across one; findings raised while this bundle is open go to `.ngrace/scratch/staged-findings.md` under the next staged number, never into the record under edit; no hard Constraint in this spec transcribes a scalar count of any file it changes — every criterion below asserts a relation its instrument can observe), `D11` (nothing is deferred here; the staged entries' owners are named in NonGoals), `D27` (nothing is approved unread; ratification is the maintainer's). The payment set is exactly empty: no token is paid by this bundle, and none can be — the payer map at this commit mints 87 tokens from registry rows in both layers, already names `F233` and `F234` to the archived `C-TAUGHT-RULES` row, and names none of `F230`, `F235`, `F236`, `F237`, `D38` (measured with the shipped `derivePayerMap` over the real archive and both registry layers). The wave-1 move's stamps are the shipped writer's, derived from that map — not this bundle's payment.

Order, ceiling, and CI. The committed sequence is: (1) wave 1 — the flush of f233 and f234 (findings first, then the two index `<Entry>` lines), `--rewrite-roots` after the hand write (the shipped writer; the findings base read back), the shipped validator naming exactly the two eligibility findings (a working-tree state, never a commit), one `--retire` in the same execution wave reporting `moved 2`, then validation exits 0; (2) wave 2 — the flush of f230, f235, f236, f237 and d38, `--rewrite-roots`, then validation exits 0; (3) the close — statuses `applied` on spec and plan, the bundle's directory renamed into `.ngrace/changes/archive/`, one `--retire` reporting `moved 0` (a byte-level no-op — the early return before any write, driven), then validation exits 0. Do not raise the persisted ceiling. Do not mint any row. Do not write a `<PaidBy>` — `--retire` is the sanctioned writer of the retired siblings and of the stamp. A read-back above a held ceiling stops the task and reports; it does not raise the ceiling, does not trim a staged body, and does not reorder the waves to dodge the arithmetic — the honest outcomes are flush-as-specified or stop.

Buffer handling. The flush set is closed by anchor id: an entry is flushed if and only if its anchor id is one of f233, f234, f230, f235, f236, f237 or d38, matched as anchor forms in the buffer, never by position. Bodies embed through the shipped `xmlEscape` render shape: the record `<Body>` is exactly the shipped escape of the staged body bytes, the decode round trip returns the staged bytes for every flushed body (driven over all seven), and the flush applies no other transform — no trim, no reflow, no renumber, no normalization. The staged entries' internal citations are already written in the delimiter-preserving slug form (`F9.1` is `f9.1`, never `f91`; `F136.1` is `f136.1`), and the flush must not repair them into any other form. The citation rule binds the same way: a staged cross-reference that would not resolve against the index does not enter the record — a stop-and-report, never something to normalize away at render. Nothing in this bundle writes `.ngrace/scratch/staged-findings.md`: the buffer is untracked and `.gitignore`d, so it has exactly one copy and no backup, and pruning the flushed entries remains post-merge hygiene owned by the authority, not a task here. Because the buffer can be pruned at any moment after the flush PR merges, no close-bound criterion in this spec reads it: the verbatim-embed evidence is the flush task's read-back at execution time, while the buffer still holds the entries, and the close-time instruments assert only facts that survive pruning.

Write scope, anchors, and imports — derived from the Goals, not from this list's own self-report (F227's rule, stated so the derivation is checkable), and enumerated once (F136.1's rule). The Goals force these writes, and nothing else: the record files `docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH/findings.xml`, `docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH/findings-retired.xml` (written only by the shipped `--retire`, which is the sanctioned writer), `docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH/rulings.xml` and `docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH/decisions.xml` (the wave-1 move also writes the two index layer flips inside `decisions.xml`); `scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts` (the production walk assertion the Goals charter, read-only over the record); and this bundle's own artifacts under `.ngrace/changes/active/C-FLUSH-TWO-WAVES/`. Do not mint a synthetic module, and do not repeat this list as a second module list anywhere. Do not register the record files in CONTEXT_ARTIFACTS. Do not add a lint issue code. Escape markup as character data (`<`, `>`, `&`) in every artifact this bundle writes; never paraphrase brackets away.

Criterion mapping, stated plainly (the trap that has cost supersedes). Every `AC-*` below except `AC-NO-CURRENT-MODE` is close-bound by its own `CloseEvidence` child, and a task `Satisfies` that names any of them is the shipped error (`change.close-evidence-and-satisfied`, `src/lint/catalog.ts:286`). Evidence hygiene, settled lessons. The walk assertion the later plan adds is a read-only walk over the record in the C-FLUSH-AND-UNPIN flush-invariant house shape (exactly once across the genre pair, status and index layer agreeing with the holding file, no fixed expectation of which file holds it) plus the shipped read-back arithmetic; the suite before it exists contains zero occurrences of `f230`, `f235`, `f236`, `f237` and `d38` (measured at this commit — F213's law: grep before citing), and the shipped `C-TAUGHT-RULES` carrier walk already covers `f233` and `f234`, so no assertion is invented twice and no suite repair is chartered. Each criterion names the mutation that turns its evidence red, and both directions are shown before the artifact is approved; a red-direction probe that plants or mutates a record element verifies the mutation landed before reading the result, and plants into whichever file the walk found the element in (F229's state-independent form). Every `CloseEvidence` `Command` matches a shipped discriminating shape — read at `src/artifact/grammar.ts:100`-177 (`DEFAULT_CLOSE_EVIDENCE_COMMAND_SHAPES`) and `:191`-203 (`closeEvidenceCommandIsDiscriminating`, token-based over flattened text): the bun-test shape for the suite, the grace.ts-lint shape at `--fail-on warnings` for close-time lint, and the `git diff --exit-code` shape with a named baseline commit for every byte-invariance claim (F210's rule — the base-less `git diff` form cannot fail). No criterion compares a fixed `git show` against a floating working-tree read (F215): every diff criterion's window is this bundle's own diff, stated in the criterion, probed in the post-close state, with this bundle's own archive directory excluded from archive pathspecs (F188 — the close's own rename is not a modification) and tracked paths only (F174). Structural counts are parsed, never grepped, and exit codes are read directly, never through a pipe. Any test the later plan adds that measures the real repository carries an explicit generous timeout (F185). Every task `Verification` command the later plan records must exit 0 as written at recording time (F184). Task `Verification` and `TargetAssertions` contain no current-mode lint of this project root (F171 — the shipped detector misses the grace.ts form, so the check is by hand and is the one Satisfies-mapped criterion). Current-mode lint appears only as post-archive AC-CLOSE-LINT. Payer-map measurements call the shipped `derivePayerMap`. The check that decides approval (F231's rule): every `CloseEvidence` command **and the full `bun run validate:ci`** run inside a **faithful** copy of the post-close state — the copy made by `rsync` of the working tree including untracked files (a `git clone` drops the buffer and the bundle and is not faithful), the two waves and the wave-1 `--retire` performed with the shipped commands, the close's statuses written and the bundle archived — and the retirement suite runs at three states: pre-flush at the baseline commit, after wave 1's move, and post-wave-2. A suite that is green pre-close and unmeasured post-close is unverified for the state that matters. The record's own move probe obeys the staged `F235`'s rule: a copy-drive of the record runs from inside a whole-repository copy, because the engine reads the archive from the process's cwd — a drive that copies only the record directory and runs the move from the repository root reads the copy's registry and the real archive and is refused as an instrument here.

Measured at this commit: the archived `C-TAUGHT-RULES` row already mints `F233` and `F234` (and `F210`, `F196`, `F199`, `F188`, all retired by its close), the shipped `derivePayerMap` names none of `F230`, `F235`, `F236`, `F237`, `D38`, and this bundle mints no channel — no row, no `Pays` element, no `PaidBy` stamp of its own — so the close's move reports `moved 0` and writes nothing, and a larger number is a stop, not an expectation.

AcceptanceCriteria.AC-FLUSH-LANDED:
After both waves, each flushed id — `f233` and `f234` (wave 1, retired by the same wave's move), then `f230`, `f235`, `f236` and `f237` as `<Finding>` elements and `d38` as a `<Decision>` element (wave 2) — exists exactly once across its genre's pair of files (`findings.xml` and `findings-retired.xml` for the findings; `rulings.xml` and `rulings-retired.xml` for `d38`), with no fixed expectation of which file holds it: the element's `status` agrees with the file that holds it (`live` in the live file, `retired` in the retired sibling), its token and genre agree, and the single `<Entry>` the index carries for the id has `layer` agreeing with that holding file — the relation survives the record's own payment cycle, which retires a finding, flips its index layer, and leaves every clause of the relation true (driven: wave 1's move keeps the shipped `C-TAUGHT-RULES` carrier walk green over `f233` and `f234` on the production record). The house shape (open tag, `<Title>` carrying the heading line, `<Body>` carrying the shipped escape of the staged body, close tag), the append position (after the last live element of the live file, before the root close tag; after the last existing entry in the index, in wave order), and the verbatim body bytes are the flush task's read-back at execution time, while the buffer still holds them (the buffer is pruned post-merge by the authority, so no close-time instrument reads it, and no criterion here can depend on it). Each wave's written findings root base equals the file's `newlineCount` after the write, and the index base equals its live-`Entry` count — both via `--rewrite-roots`, the shipped writer. Content question. Failure: an element missing, duplicated across the pair, or carrying a disagreeing token, genre, or index `Entry` layer; a base derived from a projection instead of the read-back; a render-time normalization beyond the shipped escape applied silently. The instrument is the production assertion the later plan adds to `scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts` (the C-FLUSH-AND-UNPIN flush-invariant house shape) over `f230`, `f235`, `f236`, `f237` and `d38`, landing with the wave-2 commit — the wave-1 state is covered by the shipped `C-TAUGHT-RULES` carrier walk over `f233` and `f234` (payment-invariant by construction) — plus the shipped `findingLineCounts` arithmetic for the read-back; the walk is the duplicate check. Shown green on the driven moved record, and shown failing on mutated copies with a `<Finding>` element duplicated (the walk reads two carriers) and with a flushed element's index layer flipped against its holding file (both driven; the layer-flip mutation also reddens the shipped roots tripwire, and the probe reads this criterion's own walk among the failures).

AcceptanceCriteria.AC-ROOTS-HELD:
The four live roots satisfy the shipped relations and no ceiling moved across the bundle: for `findings.xml`, `registry.xml`, `decisions.xml` and `rulings.xml` — `base + headroom = ceiling` and each `base` equals its shipped metric read back (`newlineCount` for findings and rulings, the live-`Entry` rule for the index, the live `Row` count for registry), observed by the shipped roots-invariant tripwire (`scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts`, the `C-PAYMENT-RECORD-4 roots invariant` test). The relations are payment-invariant by construction: the only shipped writers of the roots, `persistSnapshot` and `--rewrite-roots`, rewrite them in exactly this form — a ceiling holds or falls, never rises — so the assertion holds across every later legitimate move.
